transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-08
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Liam Harper (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Nadia Ruiz (CTO, Cinderpoint), Ethan Cole (Head of Security), Priya Desai (Platform)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focused on data exposure controls — request storage toggles, logging redaction rules, PII masking, and Dedicated pilot for low-latency ingestion. Customer is evaluating for a production telemetry + LLM feature set, strong security posture required (SOC2 + in-region data).

Topics: console toggles, API-level flags, ephemeral vs persisted request storage, redaction rules (regex, named-entity), key management (KMS / HSM), audit trails, sample retention policies, performance tradeoffs when enabling full request capture

Action items (captured verbally): see metadata field

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam: All right, thanks for joining everyone, Liam from Redwood here, I'm the AE, I'm joined by Sofia on the call, she's going to drive the console tour. Nadia, Ethan, Priya, can you hear me okay?
[00:09] Nadia: Yep loud and clear, thanks.
[00:11] Ethan: Good to go.
[00:12] Priya: Yup.
[00:15] Sofia: Cool, I'll share my screen in a sec. Quick agenda — show the data exposure controls pane in the console, show API toggles for request capture, run through a redaction rule example and talk about Dedicated pilot implications.
[00:28] Nadia: Sounds good. Our main ask is we need to prove we don't persist PII outside of our region and be able to show auditors that logs are scrubbed. Also, latency matters for real-time features.
[00:40] Sofia: Totally. We'll show region scoping for storage and the request ejection feature — sometimes we call it "selective ejection" or the console shows it as "telemetry ejection" — apologies if names differ in the docs.
[00:52] Priya: We've got ingestion peaks that hit about 1.2k RPS for synchronous calls, so curious about perf hit when we enable request capture on a per-route basis.
[01:06] Sofia: Great question. There's a cost/latency tradeoff. With capture on, we do asynchronous offload to object storage if you opt for persisted capture. For low latency we recommend ephemeral capture + KV prefix caching + model routing to smaller variants.
[01:24] Ethan: Can you show the redaction UI? We have patterns of customer SSNs, IBANs, and sometimes free-form addresses.
[01:33] Sofia: Sure — opening the Controls > Request Storage section. (screen) Here you can toggle default storage mode: Off, Ephemeral, Persisted. You can then attach redaction pipelines which are a sequence of rules — regex, named-entity (NER) based, and a manual scrub list. Unfortunately the NER tagger sometimes is transcribed in docs as "NAR" — small typo, but it's the NER module.
[01:58] Sofia: I'll add a new rule: regex for SSN pattern "\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b" — and mark action: replace with "[REDACTED_SSN]". We can preview on sample logs.
[02:14] Priya: That preview view is super useful. Can we apply rules only to certain routes?
[02:18] Sofia: Yes, you can scope by API key, by route name, or by tag. e.g., tag route /billing/* to always apply stricter redaction.
[02:29] Liam: Also note you can set per-tenant defaults if you are a Dedicated customer or when using private deployment.
[02:36] Nadia: About encryption — logs at rest need to be with customer-managed keys, is that supported?
[02:41] Sofia: Yes, KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we offer server-side encryption and an enterprise add-on for CMKs. There was a misprint in our earlier deck that called it KMC, that's KMS.
[02:55] Ethan: And HSM for key storage? We need hardware-backed keys for certain regs.
[02:59] Sofia: HSM-backed keys via our KMS integrations are available for Private deployments; we can map that out in the architecture doc I'll send.
[03:10] Nadia: Walk us through the audit logs — we need to show who accessed which request and when.
[03:16] Sofia: Sure — opening Observability > Audit Trail. The console shows user, action, resource, timestamp and we have immutable logs for X days depending on retention policy. You can configure export to SIEM (Splunk, Sumo, VectorServe) or to your GCS/S3 bucket.
[03:36] Priya: Are the audit exports themselves scrubbed or do they contain raw payloads?
[03:40] Sofia: Audit events are metadata-first — they point to request IDs. If you choose to include payload references, those are subject to the same redaction pipeline. So you control whether payloads are referenced or not.
[03:53] Nadia: Great. Any built-in PII classification or is it all rule-based?
[03:58] Sofia: We have both — you can run an automated PII classifier that's ML-backend powered (model may be labeled in UI as "PII detector") and combine that with rule-based overrides. The classifier does a decent job but we recommend human-verified training examples for edge cases.
[04:16] Ethan: How do you handle false positives on PII detection? We can't redact transaction IDs accidentally.
[04:21] Sofia: You can create allow-lists (safe fields) and create context-aware rules. Also in the console we have a review queue where flagged items are shown for manual accept/reject before applying at scale.
[04:33] Priya: Show the API toggle? We want to integrate programmatically.
[04:36] Sofia: Yep — REST endpoint is /v1/admin/settings/request_storage, and there are flags: capture_mode, redaction_profile_id, retention_days, storage_region. Liam, do we have that link?
[04:49] Liam: I'll paste in the chat, but for reference here's the sample curl we use in the demo: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/settings/request_storage -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"capture_mode":"ephemeral","redaction_profile":"rp-123"}'
[05:06] Priya: Good, we'll put that behind our config pipeline. Do you have a terraform provider?
[05:11] Sofia: Yes, there's a community provider and an enterprise module for Dedicated. The provider supports redaction profiles, route tags, and storage policies.
[05:18] Ethan: Performance numbers — you mentioned perf hit earlier. Any benchmarks?
[05:22] Sofia: Rough numbers — enabling persisted capture with heavy redaction can add ~15-40ms median and some p90 increases depending on regex complexity and NER steps. If you use ephemeral + async offload the median is often sub-10ms. We can run benchmarks in your Dedicated trial.
[05:40] Nadia: We'll need a concrete run. Our SLOs are p99 < 120ms; synchronous calls can't exceed that.
[05:47] Sofia: Totally reasonable. For p99 workloads we recommend Dedicated with local SSD caching and route pinning to reduce jitter. We'll propose a short perf run.
[05:58] Priya: Any pre-baked redaction templates for financial services?
[06:02] Sofia: Yes — templates: finance, healthcare, legal. They include common regexes, NER sets, and sample previews. I'll attach the finance template link after the call.
[06:13] Ethan: How do we prove to auditors that redaction actually ran? Do you have certificates or hashes?
[06:19] Sofia: We produce a redaction report artifact — hashes of original and sanitized snapshots are recorded with an audit entry. For Private deployments we can optionally store that artifact in your bucket.
[06:30] Liam: Quick note — retention policies are configurable per-profile. You can set delta retention for metadata longer than payloads if you need logs for metrics but not for PII.
[06:43] Nadia: Is there a way to do on-demand ejection? Like, keep ephemeral by default but persist when a legal hold is triggered?
[06:50] Sofia: Yes, we have programmatic ejection: a POST to /v1/admin/eject-requests with filters. That triggers a snapshot and runs the redaction pipeline then persists to the chosen bucket.
[07:03] Priya: That could fit our compliance flow. What about cross-region replication? We must keep data in EU for EU users.
[07:09] Sofia: Storage region is enforced at policy level; replicated copies are only allowed to regions you explicitly permit. We have a guardrail that warns if a policy would export out of allowed regions.
[07:21] Ethan: Any gotchas with the SDKs? We use the Go SDK heavily.
[07:25] Sofia: Go SDK supports request metadata tagging which is how you mark route tags and tenant id for scoping. One caveat — older SDK versions had a bug where the metadata header was truncated, but that's fixed in v0.9.4.
[07:38] Nadia: Excellent. Any network egress implications for persisted capture?
[07:42] Sofia: Persisted capture will do chunked uploads to your chosen object store — egress depends on your cloud provider. If you want to keep everything on-prem we can run Private deployment with direct mounting.
[07:54] Liam: I'm going to switch to the policy simulator — it's a quick live demo.
[07:58] Sofia: (screen) Policy simulator lets you upload a sample trace and see which rules hit, and it shows an estimated latency delta and cost estimate per thousand requests.
[08:12] Priya: Nice, can we upload sample logs?
[08:14] Sofia: Yes, drag and drop JSON or point to a GCS object. Let's test with a small sample that Priya shared earlier — (uploads) — the simulator shows three rule matches: SSN regex, address NER, and an allow-list for transaction IDs. 
[08:32] Sofia: Preview of sanitized sample: you can click to see diff, and there's an option to create a redaction profile from the validator's results.
[08:40] Ethan: That diff view will help for auditors.
[08:43] Nadia: Can you share the console recording and these snapshots after the call?
[08:47] Sofia: Yes, I'll share the recording and the simulator output.
[08:50] Liam: Next steps? We'll provision a Dedicated trial, Sofia will run a benchmark with your sample traces, and we'll send SOC2 + arch doc.
[08:59] Priya: Timeline — can we do the benchmark next week?
[09:02] Liam: Yes, aiming for Apr 13th.
[09:05] Nadia: Perfect.
[09:07] Ethan: One more question — do you have an SLA for request ejection and deletion? We need guaranteed deletion within X hours for takedown.
[09:14] Sofia: For Dedicated and Private we support contractual deletion windows; for hosted there's a standard 72-hour deletion for persisted copies, but we can offer tighter SLAs with enterprise add-on.
[09:27] Nadia: Okay we'll note that. Anything else?
[09:31] Liam: That's it from our side. We'll follow up with the resources. Thanks everyone.
[09:36] Priya: Thanks, bye.

(End of recording)
